1.text_clean:
1. Two sets of data, shown below with circles and squares, are obtained in two experiments. The size of the error bars is the same for all points.
[Graph: y from 0 to 10 against x from 0 to 4; circles at (1,4), (2,5), (3,6), (4,7) and squares at (1,2), (2,3), (3,4), (4,5), all with equal error bars; parallel best-fit lines with y intercepts 3 (circles) and 1 (squares)]
What is correct about the absolute uncertainty and the fractional uncertainty of the y intercept of the two lines of best fit?
| | Absolute uncertainty | Fractional uncertainty |
A. larger for squares | same
B. larger for squares | larger for squares
C. same | same
D. same | larger for squares

2.text_clean:
2. A large stone is dropped from a tall building. What is correct about the speed of the stone after 1 s?
A. It is decreasing at increasing rate.
B. It is decreasing at decreasing rate.
C. It is increasing at increasing rate.
D. It is increasing at decreasing rate.

3.text_clean:
3. The graph shows how the position of an object varies with time in the interval from 0 to 3 s.
[Graph: position / m (0 to 4) against time / s (0 to 3); curve increasing with increasing gradient from A (0 s, 1 m) through B (1 s, about 1.2 m) and C (about 2 s, about 2.3 m) to D (about 3 s, about 3.5 m)]
At which point does the instantaneous speed of the object equal its average speed over the interval from 0 to 3 s?

4.text_clean:
4. A car takes 20 minutes to climb a hill at constant speed. The mass of the car is 1200 kg and the car gains gravitational potential energy at a rate of 6.0 kW. Take the acceleration of gravity to be $10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$. What is the height of the hill?
A. 0.6 m
B. 10 m
C. 600 m
D. 6000 m

5.text_clean:
5. A mass is released from the top of a smooth ramp of height $h$. After leaving the ramp, the mass slides on a rough horizontal surface.
[Diagram: mass at top of a curved smooth ramp of height h, followed by rough horizontal surface; stopping distance d marked]
The mass comes to rest in a distance $d$. What is the coefficient of dynamic friction between the mass and the horizontal surface?
A. $\frac{gd}{h}$
B. $\sqrt{\frac{d}{2gh}}$
C. $\frac{d}{h}$
D. $\frac{h}{d}$

6.text_clean:
6. Masses X and Y rest on a smooth horizontal surface and are connected by a massless spring. The mass of X is 3.0 kg and the mass of Y is 6.0 kg. The masses are pushed toward each other until the elastic potential energy stored in the spring is 1.0 J.
[Diagram, seen from above: small block mass X connected by a spring to larger block mass Y]
The masses are released. What is the maximum speed reached by mass Y?
A. $0.11\ \text{m s}^{-1}$
B. $0.33\ \text{m s}^{-1}$
C. $0.45\ \text{m s}^{-1}$
D. $0.66\ \text{m s}^{-1}$

7.text_clean:
7. A force acts on an object of mass 40 kg. The graph shows how the acceleration $a$ of the object varies with its displacement $d$.
[Graph: a / m s^-2 against d / m; a constant at 10 from d = 0 to 2 m, then rising linearly to 20 at d = 4 m]
What is the work done by the force on the object?
A. 50 J
B. 2000 J
C. 2400 J
D. 3200 J

8.text_clean:
8. Which aspect of thermal physics is best explained by the molecular kinetic model?
A. The equation of state of ideal gases
B. The difference between Celsius and Kelvin temperature
C. The value of the Avogadro constant
D. The existence of gaseous isotopes

9.text_clean:
9. When 40 kJ of energy is transferred to a quantity of a liquid substance, its temperature increases by 20 K. When 600 kJ of energy is transferred to the same quantity of the liquid at its boiling temperature, it vaporizes completely at constant temperature. What is
$\frac{\text{specific latent heat of vaporization}}{\text{specific heat capacity of the liquid}}$
for this substance?
A. $15\ \text{K}^{-1}$
B. 15 K
C. $300\ \text{K}^{-1}$
D. 300 K

10.text_clean:
10. Two ideal gases X and Y are at the same temperature. The mass of a particle of gas X is larger than the mass of a particle of gas Y. Which is correct about the average kinetic energy and the average speed of the particles in gases X and Y?
| | Average kinetic energy | Average speed |
A. larger for Y | larger for Y
B. same | larger for Y
C. same | same
D. larger for Y | same

11.text_clean:
11. An object performs simple harmonic motion (shm). The graph shows how the velocity $v$ of the object varies with time $t$.
[Graph: v against t, starting at a positive maximum (cosine shape)]
The displacement of the object is $x$ and its acceleration is $a$. What is the variation of $x$ with $t$ and the variation of $a$ with $t$?
[Options A-D: pairs of sketch graphs of x against t and a against t]
A. x: sine starting at 0 and increasing; a: starting at 0 and decreasing (negative sine)
B. x: sine starting at 0 and increasing; a: sine starting at 0 and increasing
C. x: starting at negative maximum (negative cosine); a: starting at 0 and decreasing (negative sine)
D. x: starting at positive maximum (cosine); a: starting at negative maximum (negative cosine)

12.text_clean:
12. A sound wave has a frequency of 1.0 kHz and a wavelength of 0.33 m. What is the distance travelled by the wave in 2.0 ms and the nature of the wave?
| | Distance travelled in 2.0 ms | Nature of the wave |
A. 0.17 m | longitudinal
B. 0.17 m | transverse
C. 0.66 m | longitudinal
D. 0.66 m | transverse

13.text_clean:
13. Monochromatic light of wavelength $\lambda$ is incident on a double slit. The resulting interference pattern is observed on a screen a distance $y$ from the slits. The distance between consecutive fringes in the pattern is 55 mm when the slit separation is $a$.
$\lambda$, $y$ and $a$ are all doubled. What is the new distance between consecutive fringes?
A. 55 mm
B. 110 mm
C. 220 mm
D. 440 mm

14.text_clean:
14. A metal rod of length 45 cm is clamped at its mid point. The speed of sound in the metal rod is $1500\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ and the speed of sound in air is $300\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. The metal rod vibrates at its first harmonic. What is the wavelength in air of the sound wave produced by the metal rod?
A. 4.5 cm
B. 9.0 cm
C. 18 cm
D. 90 cm

15.text_clean:
15. Two charges $Q_1$ and $Q_2$, each equal to 2 nC, are separated by a distance 3 m in a vacuum. What is the electric force on $Q_2$ and the electric field due to $Q_1$ at the position of $Q_2$?
| | Electric force on $Q_2$ | Electric field due to $Q_1$ at the position of $Q_2$ |
A. $4\times10^{-9}$ N | $2\ \text{N C}^{-1}$
B. 4 N | $2\ \text{N C}^{-1}$
C. $4\times10^{-9}$ N | $2\times10^{-9}\ \text{N C}^{-1}$
D. 4 N | $2\times10^{-9}\ \text{N C}^{-1}$

16.text_clean:
16. Two conductors $S$ and $T$ have the $V/I$ characteristic graphs shown below.
[Graph: I / A (0 to 8) against V / V (0 to 8); T is a straight line through the origin to (8 V, 6 A); S is a curve through the origin rising steeply, crossing T at (4 V, 3 A) and reaching 6 A at about 5 V]
When the conductors are placed in the circuit below, the reading of the ammeter is 6.0 A.
[Circuit: cell in series with an ammeter and S and T connected in parallel]
What is the emf of the cell?
A. 4.0 V
B. 5.0 V
C. 8.0 V
D. 13 V

17.text_clean:
17. For a real cell in a circuit, the terminal potential difference is at its closest to the emf when
A. the internal resistance is much smaller than the load resistance.
B. a large current flows in the circuit.
C. the cell is not completely discharged.
D. the cell is being recharged.

18.text_clean:
18. An electron enters the space inside a current-carrying solenoid. The velocity of the electron is parallel to the solenoid's axis. The electron is
A. slowed down.
B. speeded up.
C. undeflected.
D. deflected outwards.
18.note: Official key (verified in markscheme PDF) is A, but the field inside a solenoid is parallel to its axis, so for v parallel to B the magnetic force qv x B is zero: the electron is undeflected and its speed does not change (a magnetic force never does work). Correct answer should be C.

19.text_clean:
19. A child stands on a horizontal rotating platform that is moving at constant angular speed. The centripetal force on the child is provided by
A. the gravitational force on the child.
B. the friction on the child's feet.
C. the tension in the child's muscles.
D. the normal reaction of the platform on the child.

20.text_clean:
20. A simple model of an atom has three energy levels. The differences between adjacent energy levels are shown below.
[Diagram: three energy levels; gap between top and middle $6.63\times10^{-19}$ J, gap between middle and bottom $13.3\times10^{-19}$ J]
What are the two smallest frequencies in the emission spectrum of this atom?
A. $0.5\times10^{15}$ Hz and $1.0\times10^{15}$ Hz
B. $0.5\times10^{15}$ Hz and $1.5\times10^{15}$ Hz
C. $1.0\times10^{15}$ Hz and $2.0\times10^{15}$ Hz
D. $1.0\times10^{15}$ Hz and $3.0\times10^{15}$ Hz

21.text_clean:
21. What is the relation between the value of the unified atomic mass unit in grams and the value of Avogadro's constant in $\text{mol}^{-1}$?
A. Their ratio is 1.
B. Their product is 1.
C. Their sum is 1.
D. Their difference is 0.
21.note: Mole/Avogadro concept (B.3) vs unified mass unit (E.3); chose B.3.

22.text_clean:
22. In a hydrogen atom, the sum of the masses of a proton and of an electron is larger than the mass of the atom. Which interaction is mainly responsible for this difference?
A. Electromagnetic
B. Strong nuclear
C. Weak nuclear
D. Gravitational
22.note: Mass defect / binding energy (E.3); also touches fundamental interactions (X.2).

23.text_clean:
23. Which Feynman diagram describes the annihilation of an electron and its antiparticle?
[Options A-D: Feynman diagrams with time axis to the right. A: two incoming fermion lines meeting at a vertex, upper arrow forward and lower arrow backward in time, producing an outgoing photon. B: two incoming lines both with arrows forward in time producing a photon. C: incoming line with arrow pointing backward and outgoing line with arrow forward, photon emitted at vertex. D: incoming and outgoing lines both with arrows pointing backward, photon emitted at vertex]

24.text_clean:
24. Burning one litre of gasoline produces more energy than burning one kilogram of coal, and the density of gasoline is smaller than $1\ \text{g cm}^{-3}$. What can be deduced from this information?
A. Energy density is greater for gasoline.
B. Specific energy is greater for gasoline.
C. Energy density is greater for coal.
D. Specific energy is greater for coal.

25.text_clean:
25. Which change produces the largest percentage increase in the maximum theoretical power output of a wind turbine?
A. Doubling the area of the blades
B. Doubling the density of the fluid
C. Doubling the radius of the blades
D. Doubling the speed of the fluid

26.text_clean:
26. Which is correct for the tangential acceleration of a simple pendulum at small amplitudes?
A. It is inversely proportional to displacement.
B. It is proportional to displacement.
C. It is opposite to displacement.
D. It is proportional and opposite to displacement.

27.text_clean:
27. The diagram shows the diffraction pattern for light passing through a single slit.
[Graph: relative intensity (central maximum 1) against diffraction angle / $10^{-2}$ rad from -2 to 2; first minima at -1 and +1, secondary maxima near ±1.5]
What is $\frac{\text{wavelength of light}}{\text{width of slit}}$?
A. 0.01
B. 0.02
C. 1
D. 2

28.text_clean:
28. Light is incident on a diffraction grating. The wavelength lines 600.0 nm and 601.5 nm are just resolved in the second order spectrum. How many slits of the diffraction grating are illuminated?
A. 20
B. 40
C. 200
D. 400

29.text_clean:
29. On approaching a stationary observer, a train sounds its horn and decelerates at a constant rate. At time $t$ the train passes by the observer and continues to decelerate at the same rate. Which diagram shows the variation with time of the frequency of the sound measured by the observer?
[Options A-D: graphs of frequency measured by observer against time, dashed line at horn's frequency, sudden drop at time t. A: above horn's frequency and increasing before t, below and decreasing after t. B: above and decreasing before t, below and decreasing after t. C: above and increasing before t, below and increasing after t. D: above and decreasing before t, below and increasing towards the horn's frequency after t]

30.text_clean:
30. A particle with charge $-2.5\times10^{-6}$ C moves from point X to point Y due to a uniform electrostatic field. The diagram shows some equipotential lines of the field.
[Diagram: parallel horizontal equipotential lines labelled 100 kV, 200 kV, 300 kV, 400 kV, 500 kV, 600 kV, 700 kV from top to bottom; X on the 300 kV line, Y on the 700 kV line]
What is correct about the motion of the particle from X to Y and the magnitude of the work done by the field on the particle?
| | Motion of the particle from X to Y | Magnitude of the work done by the field on the particle |
A. uniform linear | 0 J
B. uniform linear | 1 J
C. uniformly accelerated | 0 J
D. uniformly accelerated | 1 J

31.text_clean:
31. Which is a correct unit for gravitational potential?
A. $\text{m}^2\,\text{s}^{-2}$
B. J kg
C. $\text{m s}^{-2}$
D. $\text{N m}^{-1}\,\text{kg}^{-1}$

32.text_clean:
32. A planet has radius $R$. The escape speed from the surface of the planet is $v$. At what distance from the surface of the planet is the orbital speed $0.5v$?
A. $0.5R$
B. $R$
C. $2R$
D. $4R$

33.text_clean:
33. A conducting ring encloses an area of $2.0\ \text{cm}^2$ and is perpendicular to a magnetic field of strength 5.0 mT. The direction of the magnetic field is reversed in a time 4.0 s. What is the average emf induced in the ring?
A. 0
B. $0.25\ \mu\text{V}$
C. $0.40\ \mu\text{V}$
D. $0.50\ \mu\text{V}$

34.text_clean:
34. The conservation of which quantity explains Lenz's law?
A. Charge
B. Energy
C. Magnetic field
D. Mass

35.text_clean:
35. A resistor designed for use in a direct current (dc) circuit is labelled "50 W, 2 Ω". The resistor is connected in series with an alternating current (ac) power supply of peak potential difference 10 V. What is the average power dissipated by the resistor in the ac circuit?
A. 25 W
B. 35 W
C. 50 W
D. 100 W

36.text_clean:
36. A capacitor of capacitance $X$ is connected to a power supply of voltage $V$. At time $t = 0$, the capacitor is disconnected from the supply and discharged through a resistor of resistance $R$. What is the variation with time of the charge on the capacitor?
A. $\frac{X}{V}e^{-RXt}$
B. $\frac{X}{V}e^{-\frac{t}{RX}}$
C. $XVe^{-RXt}$
D. $XVe^{-\frac{t}{RX}}$

37.text_clean:
37. What is a consequence of the uncertainty principle?
A. The absorption spectrum of hydrogen atoms is discrete.
B. Electrons in low energy states have short lifetimes.
C. Electrons cannot exist within nuclei.
D. Photons do not have momentum.

38.text_clean:
38. In a photoelectric effect experiment, a beam of light is incident on a metallic surface W in a vacuum.
[Diagram: evacuated tube with photosurface W illuminated by a beam of light, electrons e- travelling to the collector; ammeter A measuring current I; variable supply with voltmeter V across the tube]
The graph shows how the current $I$ varies with the potential difference $V$ when three different beams X, Y, and Z are incident on W at different times.
[Graph: I against V; three straight lines rising from the V axis at negative V; X starts at a more negative V, Y and Z start at the same less negative V, with Y steeper than Z]
I. X and Y have the same frequency.
II. Y and Z have different intensity.
III. Y and Z have the same frequency.
Which statements are correct?
A. I and II only
B. I and III only
C. II and III only
D. I, II and III

39.text_clean:
39. The graphs show the variation with time of the activity and the number of remaining nuclei for a sample of a radioactive nuclide.
[Graphs: activity / Bq against time / s (0 to 6), starting at about $0.7\times10^6$ Bq and decaying exponentially; number of remaining nuclei against time / s (0 to 6), starting at $1\times10^6$ and decaying exponentially]
What is the decay constant of the nuclide?
A. $0.7\ \text{s}^{-1}$
B. $1\ \text{s}^{-1}$
C. $\frac{1}{0.7}\ \text{s}^{-1}$
D. $1.5\ \text{s}^{-1}$

40.text_clean:
40. What was a reason to postulate the existence of neutrinos?
A. Nuclear energy levels had a continuous spectrum.
B. The photon emission spectrum only contained specific wavelengths.
C. Some particles were indistinguishable from their antiparticle.
